transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-27
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Evan Cole (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Glacier - Head of ML), Tom Becker (Infra Lead), Sara Nguyen (CPO)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in; Glacier is evaluating a modest top-up of reserved capacity, adding EU region for latency-sensitive features, and wants clarity on private/VPC path for data residency. They asked for latency/cost benchmarks and security proofs (KMS/HSM, SOC2).

Topics:
- Current throughput and peak token qps
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs
- Latency SLOs in EU vs US regions
- Contract amendment options and pricing tiers
- Security/compliance attachments (KMS, audit logs, SOC2 scope)

Action items (also in metadata):
- Priya to send pricing worksheet and draft contract amendment
- Evan to run benchmark across us-west + eu-west and share spreadsheet
- Customer to share sample payload and compliance contact

Transcript body:
[14:00] Priya Shah: ok everybody thanks for joining, I know we've got a full agenda today, I'll just kick us off, um this is the renewal + regional activation check in for Glacier FinTech. Evan from our SE team is here to go over the latency and capacity bits.
[14:01] Maya Patel: hi, thanks, yes let's — appreciate it. Quick context: our current committed capacity is handling model ops fine but we see degraded tail latency for EU users especially during peak mornings. We're exploring a small uplift and a eu region activation.
[14:01] Evan Cole: yeah hi Maya, Tom, Sara. I had a look at the traffic pulse you shared last week, th-there's a clear morning spike. We can talk options — dedicated pools in eu-west or a hybrid: host primary in us with eu-edge for low latency.
[14:02] Tom Becker: just to be clear on constraints — legal wants data residency in EU for certain PII flows; infra prefers leaving model weights in Redwood-hosted but route inference in eu. Is that doable?
[14:02] Priya Shah: short answer yes, with Redwood Private or VPC we can give you control of region placement. For Hosted we do region placement too but if you need full residency and customer-managed keys we recommend Private (or Dedicated with VPC).
[14:03] Sara Nguyen: cost is a concern. If we move to Dedicated in EU, what's the delta vs just spinning up a second hosted region for routing?
[14:04] Evan Cole: good question — hosted eu region is faster to activate and cheaper initially but you get multi-tenant routing; Dedicated gives isolated GPUs and predictable throughput and SLOs, but commit costs are higher. There's also the middle ground of Dedicated burst capacity with Hosted fallback — we can model that.
[14:05] Maya Patel: for our SLA we need both 99.9% up and p95 latency < 180ms for interactive flows in EU. Does Redwood have customers hitting that with the same model sizes?
[14:05] Evan Cole: yes, we have examples. We can run a mimic benchmark with your payload. note: perf depends on batch sizes and kv cache behavior — sometimes the KV cash (transcript: kv cash) effects cause higher tail latency, we'll instrument to show that.
[14:06] Priya Shah: also to call out Redwood Optimize suggestions can lower token cost by ~20% via batching and quantization profiles — we can include that in the cost model.
[14:07] Tom Becker: security — legal asked about KMS integration and HSM support, and whether audit logs show token-level usage. Also, SOC2 and iso requirements — do you have SOC2 Type II?
[14:07] Evan Cole: we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 — I'll attach our security pack. KMS integrations are supported for Private deployments; HSM can be integrated per contract. Hosted also supports redwood-managed KMS but for full control go Private. Audit logs and the Console provide token-level breakdowns.
[14:08] Maya Patel: great. On the technical side if we do Dedicated, how fast can you provision a cluster in eu-west and what's the commit minimum?
[14:08] Priya Shah: provisioning is about 2-4 weeks depending on GPU availability and any dedicated networking work. Commit minimums vary with region and cluster size — for a mid-tier Dedicated plan it's typically a 3-6 month minimum on the initial tranche, or annual for better rates — I'll include specifics in the amendment.
[14:09] Sara Nguyen: timeline wise, we need EU activation by mid-September to align with product release. Is that feasible?
[14:09] Evan Cole: mid-September is tight but doable if we start provisioning next week and you provide network/peering info fast. Otherwise the hosted eu option can be activated in a few days for initial traffic.
[14:10] Tom Becker: another angle — we'd like to keep model weights in US for now for cost reasons, and just run inference in EU; is cross-region KV cache-heavy? Will that blow up latency?
[14:10] Evan Cole: remote KV access is expensive for latency-sensitive paths. If you're keeping weights in US but routing inference in EU, you want a model variant or quantized copy in EU. Redwood supports automated fallback to compatible model variants to reduce cross-region hops. We'll test both approaches in the benchmark.
[14:11] Maya Patel: ok, for the benchmark we can supply a sample stream and our payloads. What exact artifacts do you need?
[14:11] Evan Cole: a 24-hour capture is ideal but even representative 1-2 hour traces with peak-minute samples + typical prompts are fine. Also please indicate peak qps and average context window sizes.
[14:12] Priya Shah: and we'll include a pricing model showing hosted eu vs dedicated eu with commit and burst scenarios. We can also show per-token cost deltas with Redwood Optimize suggestions.
[14:13] Sara Nguyen: on contract — we'd prefer a 6 month bridge with option to convert to annual Dedicated after the first quarter. Thoughts?
[14:13] Priya Shah: totally something we do — we can draft an amendment that starts with a 6-month commitment for the eu nodes and rollover options to annual with discounts. I'll circulate a draft.
[14:15] [14:15] Evan Cole: quick tech deep dive — for throughput sizing, at 1500 peak qps with model size M we recommend a 3-GPU Dedicated pool in eu-west for stable p95 latency, or 1-2 xenon-class nodes with optimized batching if you want lower commit. We'll validate exact numbers in the benchmark.
[14:17] Tom Becker: network: we'll need peering and VPC endpoints for Private. Any specific firewall rules?
[14:17] Evan Cole: just allow outbound to our control plane (we'll provide IP ranges) and setup VPC peering for the Dedicated route. For Private on-prem we'll need additional connector work. I'll include a runbook.
[14:20] Maya Patel: compliance contact — who should we loop in? Sara: from legal?
[14:20] Sara Nguyen: I'll put in Alina from Legal, she'll expect KMS/HSM detail and SOC2 attestations.
[14:22] Priya Shah: next steps recap — I'll send pricing and the amendment draft by 2026-07-29, Evan will run benchmark and demo failover on 2026-08-05, and Glacier will share payload and compliance contact by 2026-07-30.
[14:23] Maya Patel: sounds good. One more Q: competitor risk — if we need a super low latency path we may evaluate self-hosting with Megatron or Anthropic private clusters; how aggressive are your SLAs and price breaks?
[14:24] Priya Shah: we can create a comparative TCO over 12 months that includes self-hosted ops costs vs Redwood Dedicated. In many cases Dedicated ends up being cheaper once you include ops and SRE overhead but we'll show the math.
[14:28] Evan Cole: small note — some of the transcription in the artifact last week said "Redwood Dedicate" which I think confused legal; it's Dedicated, the product name is Redwood Dedicated, and Private is Redwood Private. Also KV cache sometimes got transcribed as KV cash in their doc.
[14:30] Tom Becker: lol noted, transcriptions are annoying.
[14:35] [wrap-up]
[14:35] Priya Shah: ok closing — thanks everyone. We'll follow-up with attachments: security pack, pricing worksheet, and we'll schedule the benchmark run.
[14:36] Sara Nguyen: thank you.
[14:36] Maya Patel: thanks all.

References/attachments mentioned:
- Security pack (SOC2, ISO27001, KMS/HSM notes) — Redwood to attach
- Pricing worksheet (hosted vs dedicated vs hybrid) — Priya to send
- Benchmark spreadsheet template — Evan to use and return

End of transcript.
